content: This is a microscopic view of stem tissue with numerous small dark specks/dots scattered throughout bleached fibrous tissue. This pattern suggests fungal structures (sclerotia or pycnidia) in stem tissue. Top candidates: **Charcoal_Rot** (microsclerotia) or **Diaporthe/Phomopsis** (pycnidia in stem).

The test image is a microscopic close-up of split stem tissue showing **numerous tiny black microsclerotia** uniformly scattered throughout bleached fibrous pith/vascular tissue. This is the hallmark diagnostic feature of Charcoal Rot (*Macrophomina phaseolina*).

- Charcoal Rot reference shows bleached/gray stems — internally covered with tiny black sclerotia matching the test image exactly
- Diaporthe shows stem cankers at the macro level, not internal sclerotia
- Phomopsis shows pod symptoms with pycnidia on pod surfaces
